name: Noonan-like Syndrome with Loose Anagen Hair
aliases: Noonan Syndrome with Loose Anagen Hair

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Noonan-like Syndrome with Loose Anagen Hair Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of pathogenic SHOC2 gene mutation
Clinical features consistent with Noonan syndrome including characteristic facial dysmorphisms
Loose anagen hair characterized by easily pluckable, sparse, thin hair with abnormal hair root morphology
Presence of congenital heart defects such as pulmonic stenosis or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
Postnatal growth retardation or short stature

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Pathogenic SHOC2 mutation plus presence of Noonan syndrome features and loose anagen hair
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular genetic testing is essential for confirmation; clinical diagnosis may be suspected based on phenotype.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Loose anagen hair with abnormal hair root morphology
pathognomonic.notes: Hair is sparse, thin, and easily pluckable
Includes hypertelorism, downslanting palpebral fissures, and low-set ears

common.symptomName: Congenital heart defects (e.g., pulmonic stenosis, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy)
Developmental delay or mild intellectual disability

occasional.notes: Skin fold of the upper eyelid

laboratory: Possible mild anemia secondary to feeding difficulties
imaging: Echocardiogram showing pulmonic stenosis or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
Brain MRI typically normal or nonspecific
genetic: Pathogenic heterozygous mutation in SHOC2 gene (commonly c.4A>G, p.Ser2Gly)
Noonan syndrome-related RASopathy gene panel testing
other: Hair microscopy showing loose anagen hair with misshapen hair roots

distinguishingFeatures: Mutations in PTPN11, SOS1, RAF1 rather than SHOC2
More severe developmental delay and predisposition to tumors
Distinctive craniofacial features without loose anagen hair

redFlags: Severe congenital heart defects requiring early intervention
references: Cordeddu V, et al. Mutation of SHOC2 promotes aberrant protein N-myristoylation and causes Noonan-like syndrome with loose anagen hair. Nat Genet. 2009.
Tartaglia M, Gelb BD. Noonan syndrome and related disorders: genetics and pathogenesis. Annu Rev Genomics Hum Genet. 2005.
Allanson JE. Noonan syndrome. J Med Genet. 1987.
